angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 60,317,190 km at 45696.60 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 2549: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 45696.6 +/- 2200.1 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 45696.6 +/- 2200.1 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax -0.0019 +/- 0.0158 mas (same row, RUWE 1.40), -0.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 86.7 +/- 4.2 solar radii from Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 2549: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 86.7 +/- 4.2 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 60,317,190 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5625 +/- 153 K from Groenewegen & Lub (2023), A&A 676, A136, VizieR J/A+A/676/A136/table1, Name=LMC2023, columns Teffp, e_Teffp: Teff 5625 +/- 153 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07559). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Groenewegen & Lub (2023), A&A 676, A136, VizieR J/A+A/676/A136/table1, Name=LMC2023, columns Teffp, e_Teffp: Teff 5625 +/- 153 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07559)
limbDisplayGravitySource: no gravity of this star is published (none in SIMBAD); Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra) gives the class's range, log g -1.33 to 2.86. Across log g 0 to 2.85, the part the grid covers, the limb laws differ by at most 1.9% of the centre brightness from the one drawn, at log g 0.4, the gravity closest to all of them; log g 0.4 is a display choice, not a measurement (https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/VizieR?-source=J/AJ/156/171/table3)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
